MPWR is a reference power-management leader with explicit AI/server application evidence, but market cap and attention level make it less suitable for the underfollowed lane.

VSH is a strong underfollowed candidate for follow-up because its passive/discrete portfolio maps directly to AI-server power delivery and optical-networking components, but AI-specific revenue contribution must be quantified.
BELFB is a lower-confidence underfollowed candidate: product categories map to power, protection, connectivity, and magnetics, but direct AI-server or datacenter customer evidence is still missing.

Need a separate non-US or OTC pass to compare Murata, TDK, Taiyo Yuden, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Yageo, and other Asian passive-component suppliers for high-end MLCC capacity and qualification bottlenecks.
VICR should be tracked as a relatively pure US-listed AI accelerator power-delivery candidate, but it now screens as large-cap rather than the preferred USD 300M-10B underfollowed bucket.

BELFB is a stronger underfollowed discovery-lane candidate for data-center power/connectivity components; the next filter must prove AI-server or hyperscale revenue exposure rather than generic data-center participation.
VSH remains a speculative-shadow passive-component candidate: product breadth fits the node, but AI-server high-end MLCC or power-delivery qualification evidence is not yet established.

For this node, the likely chokepoint is not broad passives but high-end MLCCs, polymer/tantalum capacitors, high-current inductors, current-sense components, and compact 48V/point-of-load power modules qualified for AI accelerator boards.

Need a follow-up search on US-listed or OTC ADR suppliers for polymer/tantalum capacitors, high-current inductors, TLVR/vertical power delivery, and AI-server connector suppliers; current evidence is strongest for Murata and Vicor, weaker for Vishay.
MRAAY should remain the reference anchor for AI-server MLCC and compact power-module demand, but it is not the main underfollowed lane because it is a large established global component leader.

VICR is the strongest US-listed direct power-delivery candidate for AI accelerator/server power, but the next layer must separate durable product revenue from litigation/IP and customer-concentration noise.

VSH is a plausible underfollowed broad-component beneficiary because it combines capacitors, inductors, MOSFETs, and AI-related power demand commentary, but direct high-end AI-server component evidence remains unverified.
BELFB enters as a speculative shadow candidate: the product categories fit power/magnetics/connectivity chokepoints, but gathered evidence does not yet prove AI-server or hyperscaler exposure.

Layer 2 should search specifically for AI-server MLCC, polymer capacitor, power inductor, VRM, connector, and power-module design-ins by server ODMs and hyperscalers; broad component revenue growth is insufficient evidence.

Murata/MRAAY should remain the reference anchor for the AI-server high-end MLCC sub-node, but it is not the main underfollowed U.S. discovery candidate because it is a large non-U.S. primary-listed component leader.

Vishay/VSH is a plausible underfollowed U.S.-listed second-order candidate for AI-server board-level power delivery via power inductors, capacitors, and discrete power components; direct AI-server revenue evidence is still required.

Bel Fuse/BELFB is a plausible underfollowed U.S.-listed candidate for data-center power/connectivity/magnetics exposure, especially around 48V distribution, power shelves, redundant power supplies, and connector modules.

Vicor/VICR has cleaner direct AI accelerator power-delivery mapping than most small/mid-cap names, but its market cap and attention level are higher; keep it as a pure-play power-delivery context name rather than an obscure-passives name.

Need a follow-up pass on U.S.-traded ADR/OTC passive-component leaders such as TDK, Taiyo Yuden, Yageo/KEMET, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, and Panasonic Industry to determine whether any are investable through U.S. tickers and whether AI-server MLCC/polymer-capacitor exposure is more direct than VSH/BELFB.

For this node, the highest-quality evidence to survive Layer 2 should be explicit AI-server/datacenter revenue acceleration, high-end MLCC or power-component capacity constraints, customer qualification cycles, ASP/mix improvement, backlog, or capex tied to server power-density demand.

node: AI-server high-end passives and board-level power delivery
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for AI-server high-end passives and board-level power delivery. The reference lane is anchored by Murata for high-end MLCCs and Monolithic Power Systems for AI/server power-management ICs. The underfollowed lane adds Vishay and Bel Fuse as smaller US-listed component suppliers with plausible exposure through capacitors, inductors, resistors, power solutions, magnetic components, and connectivity, but their AI-server revenue purity still requires verification. Layer 1B expands the AI-server passives and board-level power-delivery node into a two-lane universe. The strongest reference evidence points to Murata as a high-end MLCC leader, while the underfollowed discovery lane is more investable through US-listed power-delivery and component suppliers such as Vicor, Bel Fuse, and Vishay. The key chokepoint to verify is whether AI-server demand is creating tightness in high-capacitance low-ESR/low-ESL MLCCs, polymer/tantalum capacitors, power inductors, 48V/vertical power-delivery modules, and data-center power/connectivity components rather than broad commodity passives. Layer 1B expands the US-tradable universe for AI-server high-end passives and board-level power delivery. The reference lane is Murata, because official materials and recent reporting directly connect AI-server demand to capacitors, server power modules, and MLCC capacity tightness. The underfollowed lane favors US-listed or US-traded component suppliers one or two steps away from GPUs: Vicor for high-current AI accelerator power modules, Vishay for broad passive/disc
